title: NEB Class 12 Physics — Electromagnetic Induction — 2024
subject: physics
source: NEB Grade 12 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: State Faraday's laws of electromagnetic induction and explain Lenz's law as a consequence of energy conservation.
questions.solution:
**Faraday's laws:** (i) whenever the magnetic flux linked with a circuit changes, an emf is induced; (ii) the magnitude of the emf equals the rate of change of flux, |e| = dΦ/dt. For a coil of N turns, e = −N dΦ/dt.

**Lenz's law:** the induced current opposes the change producing it. If it aided the change, the flux would grow without limit and give free energy; the work done against the opposition appears as electrical energy, so Lenz's law is energy conservation in electromagnetic form.
questions.knowledgeNote: The minus sign in e = −N dΦ/dt is Lenz's law written mathematically.

questions.question: Derive the expression for the motional emf induced in a rod of length l moving with velocity v perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field B, and find the induced current if the rod slides on rails closed by a resistance R.
questions.solution:
Each free charge q in the rod experiences force qvB along the rod, so work per unit charge (the emf) is

**e = Bvl** = Bvl (since e = ∫(v×B)·dl and v ⊥ B ⊥ l).

If the rails are closed by resistance R and the rod resistance is negligible, I = e/R = **Bvl/R**, and the power dissipated I²R equals the mechanical power Fv with F = BIl — energy bookkeeping confirms the result.
questions.knowledgeNote: Force needed to keep the rod moving at constant v is F = B²l²v/R, since the induced current produces a retarding magnetic force (Lenz).

questions.question: What is self-inductance? Derive the energy stored in an inductor carrying current I.
questions.solution:
**Self-inductance** L of a coil is the flux linkage per unit current, e = −L dI/dt, measured in henry.

While the current grows, the source does work against the back emf: dW = −e·I dt = L I dI.

Integrating from 0 to I: **U = ½LI²**, stored in the magnetic field.
questions.knowledgeNote: Compare U = ½LI² (magnetic, inductor) with U = ½CV² (electric, capacitor) — a common comparison question.
